Area.evidence_source: In several of the interviews, the suicide attempt was referred to as 'the event' and 'a bit like a taboo', i.e. not something to talk about with everybody. Suicide as a topic is actually intimate in that it requires a certain amount of confidence to be able to talk about it, one person said. Several spoke of suicide attempts as a morally objectionable act, as 'painful or embarrassing', or as the interviewee below says:; You are a loser, indeed, if you try to commit suicide... I felt so untalented, not having managed to do it this time either, and I was extremely angry at myself because I didn't manage, that you don't cope after two attempts in a row.; Several persons tell about their experiences when it comes to attitudes and lack of knowledge about mental illness prevalent in society. 'To be faced with the fact that depression is considered similar to madness makes it difficult to be open about the subject', one interviewee said. 'When you're far way down, it doesn't take much'. To be met by gazes that signalize 'poor little you' will be perceived as disgusting and degrading.; They tell about guilt from the burden that they have inflicted on children, spouses, siblings, parents and others through the suicide attempt. To this one interviewee, the suicidal attempt was regarded as almost unforgivable, in other words something that cannot be equated with other crazy things one does in life:; You don't clean up at all, you just create a hell for many others... the feeling of guilt to my family, my kids and my wife. I don't think I ever will get rid of it. Because, what I've done... I think I just have to accept that I have guilt, that I feel very guilty, I don't think I'm able to get rid of this feeling of guilt, ever. I think it's just something I have to accept, and that's it, although, as you say, your family will forgive you, however, you are not able to forgive yourself.
